problem.text: The chat example previously sent each entered prompt into conversation context without a clipboard command. This change adds local commands for copying code and exiting.

reasoning.text: Intercepting commands before context insertion avoids tokenizing or generating a response to /cc. Keeping the last response separately also allows copying after amnesia mode clears conversation context.

impact.text: pyperclip becomes an unpinned example dependency and is imported eagerly through chat_util, even when copying is not requested. The package and imported module share the name pyperclip; a whole-parent-tree search found no prior occurrences, without ruling out dynamic or external use.

source_notes.text: PR #22, “OpenAI compatible API example,” discusses an API endpoint and reuse of chat.py prompt formatting. Its shared chat.py reference is contextual overlap, not evidence that it motivated clipboard support.

Issue #16, “RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument,” reports conversion failure and discusses tokenizer truncation. Its contents do not establish a relationship to this clipboard change.

limitations: No chat session or system clipboard backend was executed. The standard-library check transcribed extraction and feedback logic, not repository execution or clipboard integration.
Clipboard backend availability and platform requirements are unestablished. The new helper does not catch exceptions from pyperclip.copy.

chapters.title: Copy the last response’s fenced code

claims.text: main initializes response to an empty string and retains the existing update from s.all_text.strip() after generation. Both streamers accumulate response text separately from presentation; the rich streamer's initial thinking branch instead accumulates think_text, so /cc searches retained response text rather than rendered terminal output.

Only input beginning immediately with '/' enters command handling; it is then stripped for exact matching. /x exits, /cc copies, and other slash-prefixed input produces an unknown-command error rather than reaching the model. Copy and unknown-command paths continue without replacing the last response.

copy_last_codeblock uses a DOTALL regex for triple-backtick fences with an opening-header newline, selects the last complete match, strips its surrounding whitespace, and calls pyperclip.copy. It returns None when no match exists. This is a lightweight extractor rather than a full Markdown parser; it neither handles tilde fences nor preserves boundary whitespace.
The caller reports newline-separated line count for a nonempty snippet, otherwise an error. New print_info and print_error helpers provide colored, prefixed feedback.

A scalar transcription selected the second of two blocks and counted two lines; unmatched and unclosed examples returned None. It also showed that strip removes first-line indentation while leaving subsequent indentation, and that a whitespace-only block yields an empty string.

findings.description: An empty matched block is copied but reported as absent.
findings.trigger: Enter /cc after a response whose last matched fenced block contains only whitespace, assuming pyperclip.copy succeeds.
findings.expected_behavior: Distinguish a missing block from an empty block, with feedback consistent with whether a clipboard write occurred.
findings.actual_behavior: The helper calls pyperclip.copy('') and returns ''. main treats this as false and prints 'No code block found in last response'. Reach is the new direct /cc call in chat.main; the whole parent-tree search found no existing helper callers.

verification.description: Reimplemented the inspected regex, stripping and caller truthiness check; the empty case reached the modeled copy operation but failed the UI success test.
verification.limits: No actual clipboard operation or chat execution.

annotation.summary: Adds /cc to copy the last fenced code block and /x to exit chat, with colored feedback and a new pyperclip dependency. Inspection identifies inconsistent feedback for empty blocks.
